text: Deadlines are a part of professional life, and handling them well is a valuable skill. The first step is effective time management. Instead of seeing a deadline as a distant threat, break the project into smaller, daily tasks. This makes the work feel less overwhelming. Next, learn to prioritize. Not all tasks are equally important, so focus on the critical elements first. Sometimes, you may realize that the original scope is too large for the time you have. In that case, practice scope management by discussing which features can be simplified or postponed. Finally, don't forget communication. If you foresee a problem, inform your team or client early. An honest conversation can lead to a revised plan rather than a missed deadline.
